A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NVS-Solver. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, embedded animation frames, and appendices support comparison despite reformatting and substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 and Appendix B report original static and dynamic novel-view synthesis experiments, including quantitative comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original results on Dycheck, depth-estimator sensitivity, guidance settings, 360-degree synthesis, and additional comparisons.

M1.justification: The core sampler, adaptive weighting, and DGS/Post procedures remain unchanged. Appendix H adds a 360-degree inference extension: staged 30-, 60-, and 120-degree generation reuses synthesized frames as prompts and joins sectors through multiview warping.

E1.justification: The original Tanks and Temples, DTU, and Internet/YouTube coverage is retained. v2 adds three Dycheck scenes with widely separated input and target cameras, 360-degree synthesis, extreme zoom scenarios, and downstream mesh reconstruction.

E2.justification: v2 adds Photoconsistent-NVS to the single-view comparison in Table 1 and Appendix N, SDEdit to the inpainting comparison in Appendix G, and ZeroNVS to the 360-degree comparison in Appendix M. The original comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include LPIPS evaluation on six single-view scenes and cross-camera Dycheck evaluation using supplied depth maps with PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. Appendix O also tests one input view for the proposed method against 12 for Sparse Gaussian on Garden. Previously reported core experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained inference-step, sampling-mode, and adaptive-weight analyses, v2 adds update-rate and gradient-normalization ablations (Table 4), depth-estimator sensitivity and outlier analysis (Appendix F), and constant/linear/exponential weighting comparisons (Appendix L). Inpainting consistency, mesh reconstruction, and extreme-zoom studies provide further diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The additional quantitative tables continue reporting point estimates without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the detailed scene tables are unchanged. Substantial new results include Photoconsistent-NVS's FID of 193.87, guidance/depth ablation scores, LPIPS comparisons, and Dycheck results: the proposed method reports PSNR 15.84 and LPIPS 0.410 versus 12.68 and 0.737 for 4D-Gaussian. These are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: v2 retains the original mathematical development but adds Appendix A, Eqs. 19–35. It introduces an error comparison against inpainting-style guidance and a tangent-space/Jacobian argument claiming manifold-preserving updates. These are substantive new derivations, although their correctness and sampling attribution have inconsistencies.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same headline claims: training-free video-diffusion NVS, adaptive scene-guided score modulation, and strong performance for static and dynamic scenes. The added experiments do not redefine those stated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds manifold-based interpretations of guidance and new explanations of depth sensitivity, including the DepthAnythingV2 outlier and DINOv2's lower FID despite worse pose accuracy. It also interprets inpainting and mesh results as evidence of cross-view consistency and discusses difficulties with large viewpoint changes and depth-scale mismatch. The original runtime limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies Particle-SFM for the existing pose evaluation and documents prompt counts and angular stages for the 360-degree extension, supplied Dycheck depths, and 2D Gaussian Splatting for mesh reconstruction. The original hardware, main sampling settings, hyperparameters, and source-code URL are retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands to autoregressive view synthesis, feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction, additional diffusion-based NVS methods, and manifold-constrained guidance. Section 4.2 adds explicit novelty positioning against guidance based on image degradation models. New references supporting the added comparisons and theory extend the research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the original prose remain intact. Changes include localized explanatory rewrites, replacing many NVS-Solver references with 'our method' or 'Ours,' updated author/header text, an ethics and reproducibility statement, and an appendix contents list.

P2.justification: v2 adds an animated introductory figure, a 360-degree results figure, an ablation table, and numerous appendix plots, diagrams, comparison panels, and tables. Existing visual and quantitative appendices are retained under new labels, while conference formatting changes their placement and layout.

improvement.justification: The paired-metric/Dycheck evaluations, additional baselines, and targeted depth/guidance ablations strengthen empirical support beyond v1's validation. The net gain is limited by Appendix A's inconsistent error-bound derivation (Eqs. 27–31) and attribution of a posterior-gradient argument to DGS, which weaken the new theoretical assurances.
